sections.title: Aromatic rhizome and leafy shoots
sections.text: Ginger is a tropical perennial herb arising from a thick, branched, aromatic rhizome, which is an underground stem rather than a root. Its leafy shoots are usually about 0.6–0.9 m tall, with narrow blades; a separate short flowering shoot rises from the rhizome. The plate correctly shows the rhizome, foliage and basal flower spike.

sections.title: Culinary use
sections.text: The rhizome is the familiar ginger spice, used fresh or dried in food. This established use refers to Zingiber officinale rhizomes; ornamental plants sold as other gingers should not be assumed equivalent. The image shows sliced rhizome but does not depict a toxic part.
